quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report: consolidated H1 2026 revenue of KRW 827,080 million against KRW 685,936 million a year earlier, with operating profit of KRW 45,734 million versus KRW 4,489 million; Q2 alone delivered revenue of KRW 407,180 million and operating profit of KRW 19,290 million
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue KRW 827,080 million, operating profit KRW 45,734 million; Q2 revenue KRW 407,180 million, operating profit KRW 19,290 million

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 revenue mix: rigid PCB KRW 545,478 million (65.95%), FPCB KRW 218,235 million (26.39%), semiconductor packaging KRW 60,047 million (7.26%) and leasing KRW 3,320 million (0.40%); the parent's own PCB business is split into HDI for communications devices and Package Substrate for semiconductors, with Package Substrate named as the next growth engine on dedicated lines and continued investment, diversifying from BOC and CSP into FC-CSP, PoP and BGA SSD
quarterly_data.figure: PCB KRW 545,478 million (65.95%), FPCB KRW 218,235 million (26.39%), semiconductor packaging KRW 60,047 million (7.26%)

quarterly_data.signal: Memory-module demand: from the second half of 2025 the memory market saw explosive demand for legacy DRAM module products on top of HBM, with replacement demand for AI data centre and general server DDR5 6400bps RDIMM (16L IVH) expanding overall demand. New module concepts — CXL, MRDIMM, LPCAMM and SOCAMM2 — are being introduced and developed at global large memory customers and moving into mass production; SOCAMM2, to be mounted on NVIDIA's next-generation CPU 'Vera', is in full development at each maker, with mass production starting in earnest from 2026 and volumes expected to expand sharply
quarterly_data.figure: DDR5 6400bps RDIMM (16L IVH) replacement demand; SOCAMM2 for NVIDIA's Vera CPU ramping from 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Product readiness: Korea Circuit has completed development of module PCBs for DDR5 High Speed (6400Mbps), next-generation enterprise SSD, CXL and LPCAMM and is in early mass production; its SOCAMM2 PCB has completed development and sample approval and is now being delivered in mass production to the customer, with volume expansion expected from 2026 onwards. LPCAMM has been sampling and shipping to customers since 2024 and CXL mass production is expected to expand from 2027; RF-SSD, a high-density enterprise SSD solution, is under joint development with global large semiconductor companies. For AI servers, enterprise high-performance high-capacity SSD (EDSFF) growth is expected even as client SSD stays slow
quarterly_data.figure: DDR5 6400Mbps, CXL and LPCAMM module PCBs in early mass production; SOCAMM2 PCB approved and shipping; CXL ramp expected from 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Order backlog at 30 June 2026 of KRW 426,639 million — PCB KRW 416,663 million on 255 thousand square metres and FPCB KRW 9,976 million — against H1 orders received of KRW 1,027,468 million of which KRW 600,829 million had been delivered; the semiconductor packaging division books orders daily or weekly and carries no long-term contract backlog
quarterly_data.figure: order backlog KRW 426,639 million (PCB KRW 416,663 million, FPCB KRW 9,976 million); H1 orders received KRW 1,027,468 million

quarterly_data.signal: Utilisation in H1 2026: the parent's PCB lines ran at 77.18% (capacity 802 thousand square metres against production of 469 thousand square metres); Interflex FPCB 78.33% and Interflex Vina 91.37%, while the Signetics semiconductor packaging line ran at only 19.69% on capacity of 570,324 thousand units against production of 105,124 thousand units
quarterly_data.figure: PCB utilisation 77.18% (capacity 802 thousand sqm, output 469 thousand sqm); FPCB 78.33%; Interflex Vina 91.37%; Signetics packaging 19.69%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity investment: the board approved on 20 January 2026 an 'MSF new investment and package equipment expansion' to respond pre-emptively to memory-semiconductor and advanced-packaging market demand; a total of 99.3 billion KRW of investment (14.6% of 2024 consolidated equity) is under way and production equipment expansion is to be completed by 31 December 2026. H1 2026 purchases of property, plant and equipment were KRW 83,665 million and construction in progress rose to KRW 126,259 million from KRW 37,903 million at the start of the year
quarterly_data.figure: MSF and package equipment investment of 99.3 billion KRW (14.6% of equity) completing by 31 December 2026; H1 capex KRW 83,665 million; construction in progress KRW 126,259 million

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration: three major customers accounted for KRW 338,255 million, or 40.90% of H1 2026 consolidated revenue — customer A KRW 107,654 million (13.02%), customer B KRW 127,540 million (15.42%) and customer C KRW 103,061 million (12.46%), none of them named in the filing. In the semiconductor packaging division the company names Broadcom, ON Semiconductor and Cypress overseas and Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and LG Electronics domestically as the customers it is pursuing for order growth, focusing on higher-value FBGA, eMCP and new flip-chip line products
quarterly_data.figure: top three customers KRW 338,255 million, 40.90% of H1 2026 revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Raw materials in H1 2026 totalled KRW 310,804 million: PCB copper-clad laminate KRW 77,065 million (24.80%) from Doosan Electro-Materials and Lotte Materials; PCB chemicals KRW 146,627 million (47.18%) from LT Metal and Taiyo Ink; FPCB base material KRW 17,949 million from Doosan Electro-Materials; and for the semiconductor packaging division BGA PCB KRW 27,811 million (8.95%) from Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Haesung DS, gold wire KRW 8,510 million from LT Metal and MK Electron, and mould compound KRW 3,919 million from Samsung SDI and KCC. Domestic BGA PCB prices rose to KRW 287 thousand per thousand pieces from KRW 216 thousand in 2025, and domestic gold wire to KRW 334 thousand per kft from KRW 235 thousand
quarterly_data.figure: raw materials KRW 310,804 million; copper-clad laminate KRW 77,065 million (24.80%); BGA PCB KRW 27,811 million (8.95%); domestic BGA PCB price KRW 287 thousand per kpcs versus KRW 216 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Package substrate outlook: capacity invested since 2021 is expected to keep package-substrate supply and demand out of balance for some time, progressively separating makers that hold long-term contracts with key customers or have expanded supply into AI product lines from those that have not, and that polarisation is likely to persist until the market recovers. Rising HBM share and the growth of Chinese memory makers could also change the existing supply chain and Korean suppliers' positions by memory product line; the company says it is leaning on long-term contracts with existing key customers while continuing to expand AI-product supply. Separately, the opening of the AI market is expanding demand for server rigid-flexible PCBs

Customer-linked capacity funding: 'investment attraction repayment obligations' of KRW 152,585 million as long-term borrowings and KRW 43,347 million as current maturities at 30 June 2026, repayable between 2023 and 2032 and discounted to present value; the filing states the counterparty is withheld under the terms of the contract
quarterly_data.figure: investment-linked repayment obligations KRW 152,585 million long-term and KRW 43,347 million current
